name: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
aliases: Safe Surgery Saves Lives pilot study
question: Does introducing a 19-item WHO surgical safety checklist reduce in-hospital complications and death after noncardiac surgery?

arms.label: Care after introduction of the 19-item WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
care before introduction of the checklist

design.population: Consecutive patients aged 16 or older undergoing noncardiac surgery in designated operating rooms of eight hospitals in eight cities, four in high-income and four in low- or middle-income countries.
design.description: Prospective before-and-after study at eight hospitals

verdictNote: Complications and deaths fell after implementation; prospective before-and-after design without a concurrent control group.
takeaway: In eight hospitals, introducing the WHO 19-item Surgical Safety Checklist was followed by lower in-hospital death (1.5% to 0.8%) and major complications (11.0% to 7.0%) within 30 days than care before implementation, in a prospective before-and-after study of 7,688 patients having noncardiac surgery.

reports.label: Initial report
reports.citation: Haynes AB, Weiser TG, Berry WR, et al. "A Surgical Safety Checklist to Reduce Morbidity and Mortality in a Global Population." *N Engl J Med.* 2009;360(5):491-499. doi:10.1056/NEJMsa0810119
reports.followUp: In hospital until discharge or 30 days, whichever came first

results.measure: In-hospital rate of any major complication, including death, within 30 days (site-standardized)
results.note: Difference in percentage points derived from the published rates.
results.locator: PDF p7, Table 5; PDF p6 text

results.note: No adjustment was made for multiple comparisons. Difference in percentage points derived from the published rates.

harms.label: Surgical-site infection
harms.note: Difference P<0.001. At site 5 (a lower-income site), 20.5% before and 3.6% after.

harms.label: Unplanned return to the operating room

delivery.label: Checklist content
delivery.value: 19 items in three oral confirmations: sign in before induction of anesthesia, time out before skin incision, sign out before the patient leaves the operating room.

delivery.label: Introduction to the operating rooms
delivery.value: Introduced over 1 week to 1 month through local lectures, written materials or direct guidance, with a recorded video, a teleconference and a site visit from the primary investigators.

delivery.label: Study rooms
delivery.value: One to four operating rooms per hospital; consecutive patients aged 16 or older having noncardiac surgery.

delivery.label: Baseline safety practices
delivery.value: None of the eight hospitals had a formal pre- or postoperative team briefing or a standard plan for intravenous access in cases of high blood loss.

delivery.label: Sample size
delivery.value: Target of 500 consecutive patients per site per phase; calculated to detect a 20% reduction in complications with 80% power and alpha 0.05.

delivery.label: Observation by data collector
delivery.value: Operative data collected by direct observation for 37.5% of patients and from unobserved clinical teams for the rest.

delivery.label: Urgent cases
delivery.note: P=0.26. Urgent was surgery within 24 hours.

reports.label: Urgent operations
reports.citation: Weiser TG, Haynes AB, Dziekan G, et al. "Effect of a 19-item Surgical Safety Checklist During Urgent Operations in a Global Patient Population." *Ann Surg.* 2010;251(5):976-980. doi:10.1097/SLA.0b013e3181d970e3
reports.followUp: In hospital for up to 30 days after surgery

results.measure: Complication rate including death, in-hospital up to 30 days
results.note: Reported complication counts were 151 before and 102 after; reported rates were 18.4% and 11.7%, with 842 and 908 urgent patients in the respective cohorts. Difference in percentage points derived from the reported rates.

results.measure: Death rate, in-hospital up to 30 days
results.note: Difference in percentage points derived from the published rates.

results.measure: Adherence to six measured safety steps

delivery.label: Urgent-operation cohort
delivery.value: 1,750 consecutive patients aged 16 or older in the same eight hospitals: 842 before and 908 after the checklist; urgent meant an operation required within 24 hours of assessment to be beneficial.
